title: Spring Boot Test Framework (@SpringBootTest, @WebMvcTest, Unit Testing with JUnit & Mockito)

richText: Choose the smallest useful test scope
JUnit runs tests and provides assertions. Mockito replaces a dependency with a controlled mock. Spring Boot test annotations select how much of the application to load.
Use a plain JUnit test for a calculation, validation rule or other class with no Spring wiring. Create the object directly. This keeps the test focused and avoids application startup.
Use JUnit with Mockito when a service must react to repository results or another dependency. Mock that dependency. Assert the service’s output or exception.

Use @WebMvcTest for controller request mapping, JSON binding, validation and HTTP responses. It loads a web slice. Supply the controller’s collaborators separately. Include relevant security configuration when checking access rules.
Use @SpringBootTest when the requirement depends on application wiring or several real components. The default web environment does not start a real server. RANDOM_PORT does.
A mock cannot prove a database query, transaction rollback, email delivery or external API behavior. Use an integration test with isolated dependencies for those requirements.
Keep each test independent. Use fresh input and controlled dependencies. A passing contextLoads test proves context startup, not correctness of journal ownership.
The playlist’s testing topics cover parameterized JUnit tests and Mockito. The focused pages below contain learning examples. They are note content and are not application test files.
